name: fluoroethylene carbonate
source_citation: Kobayashi et al. (2003) J. Fluorine Chem. 120(2) 105-110
notes: Dielectric constant 78.4 measured by the authors themselves at 23 C (296.15 K); Kobayashi, Inoguchi, Iida, Tanioka, Kumase & Fukai, J. Fluorine Chem. 2003, 120(2), 105-110, Table 2 third data row, marked 'Our data' with footnote e 'At 23 C.' T_K revised 298.15 -> 296.15 because the source states 23 C. The previously stored 102 was the flash point, not a permittivity. The competing 107 leg is now read at compilation level: Ue, Sasaki, Tanaka & Morita 2014, Chapter 2 of Electrolytes for Lithium and Lithium-Ion Batteries (Springer, DOI 10.1007/978-1-4939-0302-3_2), Table 2.3 on printed page 101 lists FEC with eps_r 107, and that chapter body text on printed page 105 attributes the FEC relative-permittivity data to its reference [25], Hagiyama et al. 2008, Chem. Lett. 37, 210-211. Table 2.3 is itself a compilation attributed on printed page 100 to two Sasaki reviews (refs [4] and [5]) and carries no per-row footnote for FEC, so 107 is a compilation value relaying the Hagiyama line rather than an independent primary measurement. Hagiyama 2008 remains unread (OUP 403 / J-STAGE 404), so the row stays model_ready=false and no average is taken. Temperature-attribution conflict (recorded, no re-assignment): Nanbu, Suzuki, Yagi, Sugahara, Takehara, Ue & Sasaki 2007, Electrochemistry 75(8) 607-610, printed page 608, restates this same Kobayashi measurement as 'the relative permittivity of FEC (78.4 at 40 C)' and restates the FEC viscosity as '4.1 mPa s at 40 C', citing its own reference 4, which is Kobayashi 2003; the primary Table 2 footnote carries the superscript 'e' on both the 4.1 and the 78.4 entries and reads 'At 23 C.', re-verified visually at 600 dpi on printed page 108 (PDF page 4), so the primary governs, T_K stays 296.15 K and the 40 C restatement is logged as a downstream citation conflict, not an independent measurement. Temperature of the competing leg (both sources open access, held locally): Nambu, Takahashi, Takehara, Ue & Sasaki 2013, Electrochemistry 81(10) 817-819, printed page 817, states 'The relative permittivity of FEC (about 107 at 25 C)'; Nambu, Kobayashi, Kobayashi, Takahashi & Sasaki 2013, Electrochemistry 81(10) 820-822, printed page 820, states 'was comparable with that of FEC (about 107 at 25 C)'; both attribute the number to the same item, Hagiyama et al. 2008, Chem. Lett. 37, 210-211. The two legs therefore sit at near-identical temperatures (23 C for 78.4 versus 25 C for the 107 claim) and remain an unreconciled value conflict rather than a temperature-resolvable pair. Still no average and still no promotion.
